title: A multiplexed high-throughput platform to report pharmacologic alteration of cancer stem cell membrane potential and cell cycle state
text:
IMAT R61 Narrative
A major challenge in cancer is how to combat treatment resistant properties of cancer stem cells (CSCs) which
drive tumor recurrence and progression. Here we develop a novel high-throughput screening platform that
reports changes in CSC electrical properties and cell proliferation in response to ion channel drugs. The
changes in electrical properties and proliferation are expected to identify drugs that “reprogram” CSCs to more
treatment responsive states which can be used in combination with current or future therapies to improve
treatment responses and outcomes for cancer patients.

title: Imaging Feedback for Histotripsy Renal Tumor Ablation
text:
Our long-term objective is to develop monitoring for histotripsy with ultrafast, bubble-specific ultrasound imaging
for effective, safe, and rapid ablation of renal cell carcinoma to decrease patient morbidity and mortality. In this
project, we aim to refine and integrate ultrafast imaging onto a clinical-grade platform to facilitate rapid adoption,
and develop and test feedback algorithms in ex vivo malignant renal tissues and a relevant large animal model.

title: Regulation of striatal microcircuits by endogenous opioids as a novel mechanism underlying cocaine seeking
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because it seeks to understand how cocaine dysregulates
striatal circuit activity to affect cocaine abuse. This research will define how a history of cocaine taking alters
the synaptic plasticity of distinct intra-striatal circuits to affect neuronal excitability and drive cocaine seeking
and taking. Our work aligns with the mission of the NIDA because it seeks to define the neural circuit conse-
quences of cocaine use that underlie the continued seeking of cocaine following drug abstinence.

title: Improving the Processes around Approval, Accrual and Translational Research in Cancer Prevention Trials
text:
The Clinical Trials Offices (CTO) at many cancer centers focus on cancer treatment trials but not on cancer
prevention trials that target high-risk populations but without active cancers. Establishing and refining current
processes around CTO’s cancer prevention trials could bolster NCI’s efforts at cancer prevention.

title: Construction of in vivo mRNA delivery systems
text:
Our research program is devoted to cell-specific drug delivery platforms for the treatment of diverse
diseases. We will integrate our specialty in pharmaceutics, pharmaceutical chemistry, biomedical engineering,
materials formulation, and animal studies to design and validate new drug delivery systems. The goal is to
translate our scientific results and technological inventions into more effective drug delivery systems.

title: Multiplex and multi-omic diagnostic test for bladder cancer recurrence
text:
BCDx is a diagnostic assay that is designed and optimized to inform on the recurrence of bladder cancer from
a patient urine sample. Integration of BCDx into the standard of care is expected to identify bladder cancer
recurrence earlier and accurately, thereby improving the chances of successful treatment.

title: National Center for Translational and Developmental Proteomics
text:
The proposed National Center for Translational and Developmental Proteomics (NCTDP) will optimize an
array of new technologies that will enable highly accurate, comprehensive studies of the many different forms of
proteins (proteoforms) that underlie health and disease. The NCTDP will sustainably disseminate these new
tools to the broad biomedical research community through commercialization, publication, presentation, user
training, and implementation in shared resource facilities.

title: Excitability and Excitotoxicity in Type-I Cochlear Afferents: Synapse Structure and Function
text:
Noise trauma is a leading cause of hearing disorders for which there are no cures, underscoring the need
for prevention, but there are no FDA-approved pharmacological interventions to prevent hearing loss. We have
shown that specific neurotransmitter receptors in the cochlea can be antagonized to prevent noise trauma
while others remain active to mediate hearing, however, local delivery of drugs to a healthy cochlea is too
invasive and systemic dosing is only tolerated if side effects can be avoided. This proposal investigates the
precise molecular composition of AMPA-type glutamate receptor pore-forming and auxiliary subunits in the
cochlea, so that they may be specifically targeted with systemic pharmacology.

title: Characterizing the Mechanism of Viral Entry Initiation in HSV
text:
Herpes simplex viruses (HSV) 1 and 2 infect nearly 70% of the world population for life and typically cause as
lesions of the mouth or genitals; however, the immunocompromised also risk developing keratitis and
encephalitis. This application proposes to elucidate the mechanism of HSV entry into the target host cells. The
knowledge and insight gained from determining the mechanism of HSV entry could help identify key targets for
preventative vaccines or curative therapeutics.

title: Decoding lineage and fate specification in the C. elegans embryo
text:
In animal development the single-celled zygote divides, and its progeny differentiate to
produce an incredible diversity of cell types, but we still have much to learn about the
molecular changes that occur in cells as they divide and differentiate. This project uses
cutting-edge microscopy and genomics tools to study this process in the embryo of the
nematode C. elegans, which uses many of the same genes as humans to specify its cell
types and allows for rapid experimentation. We will focus on how regulatory genes work
in different combinations to allow cells to make different decisions during development,
how errors in these decisions are avoided, and how the timing of developmental events
is controlled.

title: An RNA Nanosensor for the Diagnosis of Antibiotic Resistance in M. Tuberculosis
text:
Successful treatment of tuberculosis infections requires the prompt and accurate diagnosis of resistance to the
full panel of antibiotics in clinical use. Here we propose a novel approach to diagnose antibiotic resistance to
bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid, pyrazinamide, and moxifloxacin using RNA hybridization detecting a
transcriptomic signature of antibiotic response. This approach circumvents the delays and biohazard of bacterial
growth-based tests and the difficulties in interpretation of DNA based methods.

title: The role of mitochondrial ATP production in liver failure
text:
Mitochondrial dysfunction is implicated in many human disease processes, including late stage liver failure. We
have created a new animal model that deletes a gene critical for mitochondrial energy production. With this
model, we will investigate the importance of mitochondrially derived energy in physiologic liver processes.

title: Fusion oncoprotein condensates in pediatric cancers
text:
We have discovered that many fusion oncoprotens (FOs) associated with high-risk pediatric cancers form
aberrant biomolecular condensates in cells and have shown for some that condensate formation is
mechanistically linked with oncogenesis. The proposed studies of additional FOs will dramatically expand
understanding of the mechanistic roles of condensates in pediatric cancers driven by FOs and provide new
directions for the development of targeted therapeutics against them.

title: Targeting Metabolic Vulnerabilities to Restore Balanced Hematopoiesis during Aging
text:
The proposed project will elucidate the metabolic underpinnings of how certain hematopoietic stem and
progenitor cells dominant the blood system in older individuals leading to increased risk of age-related disease.
The viability of therapeutics to reduce clonal dominance by targeting the metabolic pathways altered in
dominant hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells and the mechanisms by which they act will be determined.

title: Center for Research in Emerging Infectious Diseases - Epidemiology, Surveillance and Pathogenesis
text: The goal of this project is to better understand emerging viruses, including tick-borne viruses and respiratory viruses. Multiple, related viruses found in the USA, South Asia, and East Asia will be studied to better understand the potential threat they pose to American citizens domestically and abroad.

title: Social Media, Acculturation and E-cigarette Use among Mexican American College Students in South Texas
text:
Hispanic young adults, including college students, have been the targets of tobacco marketing and this trend
continues with the marketing of ENDS products on social media. Yet, we know little about the role of ENDS-
related social media on the use of ENDS products by Mexican American college students, the largest
subgroup of Hispanics. The proposed project will fill a void by examining the associations between ENDS-
related social media exposure and engagement, and ENDS use among Mexican American college students,
as well as the factors that explain and those that modify these associations.

title: Molecular Epidemiology, Emergence of Resistance, and Clinical Outcomes of NDM-E Infections
text:
New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase–producing Enterobacterales (NDM-E) are a rapidly expanding cause of
serious infections in the United States that are difficult to treat and associated with high mortality. This proposal
will define how these bacteria develop resistance to both current therapies and drugs in late-stage
development, generating knowledge essential for preserving their effectiveness. The results will guide clinical
treatment decisions, improve patient outcomes, inform future drug development, and strengthen our ability to
control the spread of antimicrobial resistance.

title: Kinematic and neural dynamics of postural instability in Parkinson’s disease
text:
Balance problems and falls are among the most common complaints in Veterans with
Parkinson’s Disease (PD), but we have no effective treatments and our ability to measure
balance and falls remains quite poor. This study uses wearable sensors to measure balance
and uses deep brain stimulation electrodes to measure electric signals from the brain in
Veterans with PD. We hope to use this data to better understand the brain pathways underlying
balance problems in PD so that we can design new treatments to improve balance and reduce
falls in Veterans with PD.

title: Live-cell super-resolution imaging of enhancer-mediated gene bursting
text:
Proper transcriptional regulation is vital for maintaining cellular balance, and disruptions in this
process have been associated with various diseases and developmental disorders. Transcriptional
condensates and distant regulatory enhancers are key players in controlling gene expression.
Gaining insights into their three-dimensional organization and function will deepen our understanding
of disease pathology and may open new avenues for therapeutic intervention.

title: Palmitoylation and Diabetes
text:
More than 11% of Americans have diabetes, a chronic and life-threatening disease associated with
heart attacks, strokes, amputations, blindness, and cancer. The most common form is type 2 diabetes,
characterized by a poorly understood process that disrupts the function of pancreatic beta cells that produce
insulin. This application is relevant to public health because it has the potential to discover new approaches to
preserving pancreatic beta cell function, which could prevent the progression of diabetes and its complications.
